data.narrative:
Aleph Surgical is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Dylan and Ryan McGuire. The target operates within Biotech & Health, a sector encompassing 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals. The company has raised $175K to date.

Stage-progression valuation applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $175K raised, yielding an implied value of $438K. This method is appropriate for early-stage biotech where financing rounds typically correlate with value creation milestones. Peer-median analysis is not applicable: while 7 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables)—a minimum of 3 datapoints is required to support median-based valuation. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied, as target revenue is not disclosed; the sector median P/S multiple is 8.1x across public peers, but lacks an input denominator for Aleph Surgical.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $372K to $503K, with a median point of $438K, derived from a single applicable method. The primary uncertainty is the absence of robust peer comparables at the seed stage within this sector. Revenue disclosure would unlock public-comp anchoring as a secondary validation method. Given the single-method derivation and narrow comparable set, this range reflects methodological constraints rather than convergence of multiple triangulation vectors.
